newsitem.title: USA: Iraq's Hamdoon says U.N. aid plan talks continue.
newsitem.headline: Iraq's Hamdoon says U.N. aid plan talks continue.

text.p: Iraq's ambassador to the United Nations, Nizar Hamdoon, said Tuesday that talks between U.N. and Iraqi government officials are continuing, though he couldn't say whether agreement on the key aid distribution plan was near.
"They are working out issues, both logistical and on political points," said Hamdoon. "But I am not aware of the outcome of today's meetings."

U.N. humanitarian coordinator Staffan de Mistura was due to meet with Iraqi government officials on Tuesday evening in Baghdad to discuss details of incorporating the U.N.'s plan to distribute aid in the three Kurdish governates in the north and Baghdad's plan for the centre and south of the country.
U.N. officials in New York did not have information about the meeting and de Mistura's staff could not be reached in Baghdad.
Ambassador Hamdoon said he was unaware of any major snags in the talks. He said he could not say when the distribution plan will be delivered to the U.N. secretary-general for approval.

Approval of the plan is necessary to allow the second round of Iraqi oil exports under the so-called oil-for-food deal which allows Iraq to sell up to $2.14 billion of oil over 180 days to buy and distribute aid under strict U.N. supervision.
The second round took effect June 8 but exports have been stalled pending approval of the plan.
